clue.text: Steer for centre of Dodge City

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
taken as written
the third of its five letters

explanation.surface: A cowboy driving a steer towards the middle of the Wild West town of Dodge City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodge City' reads as one place name, but it splits: Dodge supplies a letter and City is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is an English university city.

clue.text: One out of order supplying artillery

indicators.note: something taken out of a word is removed from it

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
an ordinance is an official order or decree

explanation.surface: Something broken down is responsible for supplying the guns.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of ORDINANCE to leave ORDNANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is the collective term for military guns and cannon, the same as artillery.

clue.text: Legitimate objects for attack — just wild animals?

blocks.note: just and fair both mean equitable
game is wild animals hunted for sport or food

explanation.surface: Asking whether only wild creatures may rightly be hunted.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the wordplay half also happens to describe what is literally hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair game is the idiom for someone or something it is acceptable to criticise or pursue.

clue.text: First-rate boy, Alan? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word is used, the rest dropped

blocks.note: a boy's name
taken as written, then cut in half

explanation.surface: Praising a lad called Alan, then ironically agreeing with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it tells you to keep only half of Alan.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal is used informally to mean splendid or excellent, as in royal treatment.

clue.text: Top-ranking official's role tracking money

indicators.note: one thing tracking another follows behind it, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: brass is northern British slang for money
a hat is a role someone wears, as in wearing two hats

explanation.surface: A senior official's job is to keep track of the funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 's stands for 'is' joining definition to wordplay. Brass for money is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass hat is slang for a high-ranking officer or official, from the gold braid on senior military caps.

clue.text: Unfortunate male, injured too, out of play

indicators.note: an unfortunate arrangement is a bad one that wants putting right, so the letters are rearranged
out suggests being put out of place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unlucky man, also hurt, is written out of a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods at the tragedy's star-crossed lovers, both of whom die.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo and Juliet is Shakespeare's tragedy, an example of a play.

clue.text: Speaks about daughter going after a boy in an innocent, naive time

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the others
going after means following, so this piece is placed later

blocks.note: says and speaks are synonyms
taken as written
a lad is a boy
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone talks of their daughter dating a young man during her carefree youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaks' wraps around everything else; 'going after' just puts the daughter behind the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad days, from Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra, is the idiom for the period of youthful inexperience.

clue.text: Against wearing that woman's waders

indicators.note: the outer word wears the inner one like clothing, so it goes around it

blocks.note: the possessive pronoun for a woman
on as in leaning on or against something

explanation.surface: Objecting to the rubber boots a woman is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waders' looks like fishing boots, which fits the surface, but means wading birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Herons are long-legged birds that hunt by wading in shallow water.

clue.text: Article on almost highest ancient city

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the definite article
best and highest both mean top in quality

explanation.surface: A piece written about a nearly supreme city of antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' means the first piece sits above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a major city of ancient Egypt, and also of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Notice what the infantry may be given

definitions.text: what the infantry may be given

blocks.note: first meaning: notice of dismissal from a job

blocks.clueFragment: what the infantry may be given
blocks.note: second meaning: literal orders for foot soldiers to set off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' is a noun in the sense of being given notice, that is, sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching orders is the idiom for dismissal, borrowed from the command for troops to move out.

clue.text: Supplier of milk products, new firm with a dray

indicators.note: new suggests something remade, so the letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A start-up business delivering milk with a horse-drawn cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairy farm keeps cows for milk and sells it on to be made into dairy goods.

clue.text: Big in molecular genetics

indicators.note: in tells you the word sits inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone important in the field of molecular genetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Big and large are straightforward synonyms for great in size.

clue.text: Article by supporter backing backer

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read in the other direction

blocks.note: the indefinite article
a leg supports a table or a body

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece written by a sponsor who funds a sponsor.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is the theatrical term for a financial backer of a show.

clue.text: Conga led off by Conservative with traditional series of steps?

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory leads off a conga line with some old-fashioned footwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Led off' looks like the Conservative heading the dance; actually 'off' signals the shuffle and 'by' places C beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog dance is a folk dance performed in wooden clogs, a traditional set of steps.

clue.text: Ship's ladder, one of a pair used on journey

blocks.note: a companion is one of a matched pair, like a glove
a way is a route or journey

explanation.surface: A ship's ladder, one of two, put to use on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A companionway is the staircase or ladder leading between decks on a ship.

clue.text: Royal Navy chaps absorbed by a spot of decorating

indicators.note: something absorbed by another is taken inside it

blocks.note: a dot is a spot
RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Sailors are soaked up in doing a bit of painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorating' works as a noun here, the act of decorating, so it matches a noun answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adornment is the act of embellishing something, the same as decorating it.

clue.text: A person with intense energy — isn't it shocking?

blocks.note: first meaning: a lively, energetic person
second meaning: a cable carrying electric current gives a jolt

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' looks like moral outrage at the person, but it means an electric shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Live wire is the idiom for a vivacious person, from an electrified cable.

clue.text: Boy's performing with jazz pianist

blocks.note: Peter's, a boy's name with the apostrophe s
a performer who is on is on stage

explanation.surface: A lad is playing alongside a jazz pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter's on, that is, Peter is performing.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Peterson was a celebrated Canadian jazz pianist.

clue.text: What kangaroo courts dispense may be unfair, and mere formality

blocks.note: surface reading: a sham tribunal hands out its verdicts

blocks.clueFragment: may be unfair, and mere formality
blocks.note: setter's reading: the result is crude and unjust, the trial only a show

explanation.walkthrough: A kangaroo court is an unofficial, biased tribunal that ignores proper procedure; the second half describes its outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough justice is punishment handed out summarily and unfairly, exactly a kangaroo court's product.

clue.text: Armed guards in prince's cortege

indicators.note: in tells you the word is tucked inside the following letters

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Soldiers protecting a royal procession.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a group of armed guards accompanying someone for protection.

clue.text: Phone from port in Alabama

blocks.note: first meaning: a cellphone in British English
second meaning: the Gulf Coast city in Alabama

explanation.surface: Making a call from a harbour town in Alabama.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile is British for a cellphone, and Mobile is Alabama's seaport city.

clue.text: Villain with cold, nurse treated

indicators.note: something treated is worked on and changed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rogue with a chill is looked after by a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest rogue, a synonym for villain.

clue.text: Part for a firearm

blocks.note: first meaning: a portion of something
second meaning: slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A component for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion, and also gangster slang for a handgun.

clue.text: He wrote A Glastonbury Romance in a Welsh county

blocks.note: first meaning: the novelist John Cowper ...
second meaning: the large county in mid-Wales

explanation.surface: A novelist wrote his Glastonbury book while living in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cowper Powys wrote that 1932 novel, and Powys is a county of mid-Wales.

clue.text: Old wood? Express an opinion

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
pine is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: Asking about aged timber, then inviting a view on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state one's view, a formal word for expressing an opinion.

clue.text: Alpine flower in weeds, lies crushed

indicators.note: crushed things are squashed out of shape, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountain flower lies flattened among the weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a white woolly-leaved plant that grows high in the Alps.

clue.text: A setter, I suspect, for a paper

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful or dodgy, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler guessing what might suit a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like a newspaper but means a written study.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written study of a subject, like an academic paper.

clue.text: Like aquatic bird following behind the rear of a ship

definitions.text: behind the rear of a ship

blocks.note: as and like both mean in the manner of
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird trailing in the wake of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical word for behind or towards the back of a vessel.
